A 27-year-old G1P0000 woman presents to her obstetrician’s office at 24 weeks gestation complaining of new hair growth on her upper lip.
She also has worsening acne that started several weeks ago.
A pelvic exam reveals an unremarkable closed cervix and a right-sided adnexal mass without tenderness.
The cardiopulmonary exam is normal, and the patient’s abdomen has a fundal height of 31 cm.
The patient’s temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), blood pressure is 121/76 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 13/min.
She has a male fetus based on her 20 week anatomy ultrasound.
The patient has a medical history of polycystic ovary syndrome.
Her pregnancy thus far has been complicated by gestational diabetes, which is managed by diet and exercise.
She now needs to shave her face every day or else thick hair appears.
